s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain and dyspnea with pericardial effusion and elevated inflammatory markers following an upper respiratory infection and minor chest trauma
salient_findings: Chest pain and dyspnea one week after recovering from an upper respiratory infection
Mild tenderness over the sternum
Moderate circumferential pericardial effusion with right atrial collapse on echocardiography
Elevated leukocyte count, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Elevated absolute eosinophil count
key_facts: 9-year-old girl with a small muscular ventricular septal defect
Presented with chest pain and dyspnea
Chest radiography showed mild cardiomediastinal silhouette enlargement and a focal opacity in the right middle lung
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a moderate circumferential pericardial effusion with right atrial collapse
No ventricular septal defect on echocardiography
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed elevated global myocardial T2 and T1 values
Moderate pericardial effusion on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
No late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging

shortlist.label: Viral myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Initial working diagnosis, supported by elevated inflammatory markers and response to ibuprofen and colchicine

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated absolute eosinophil count and pericardial effusion, suggesting eosinophilic involvement

shortlist.label: Hypereosinophilic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Significantly elevated absolute eosinophil count and presence of pulmonary nodules, raising suspicion for hypereosinophilic syndrome

shortlist.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Eosinophilia, pulmonary nodules, and history of asthma-like symptoms (not explicitly mentioned but possible given the context) make Churg-Strauss syndrome a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Postcardiac injury syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Recent history of minor chest trauma and development of pericardial effusion, making postcardiac injury syndrome a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's significantly elevated absolute eosinophil count and the presence of a moderate pericardial effusion, along with the resolution of symptoms and reduction of the pericardial effusion after treatment, but with a further rise in eosinophil count, suggest an eosinophilic etiology for the pericarditis

rejected.label: Viral myopericarditis
rejected.why: Although the patient was initially diagnosed with viral myopericarditis, the lack of fever and the significant eosinophilia are not typical for this condition

rejected.label: Hypereosinophilic syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has a high eosinophil count, there is no evidence of end-organ damage beyond the pericarditis

rejected.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
rejected.why: There is no evidence of asthma or other systemic vasculitis symptoms

rejected.label: Postcardiac injury syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not align with the typical presentation of postcardiac injury syndrome
